QF.id: AIFM CIII Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_16

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah explains to the investor-relations team why CAPM assumes investors are only compensated for systematic risk. The correct reason is:

answer.text: Systematic risk is easier to measure than unsystematic risk.
Unsystematic risk is lower than systematic risk for any well-managed fund.
CAPM excludes unsystematic risk because it's only relevant to debt instruments.
Unsystematic risk can be diversified away by holding the market portfolio, so only non-diversifiable systematic risk is priced.

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook pages 64-66 state that when investors hold the market portfolio M, which carries only systematic risk, they need only be compensated for bearing systematic risk because unsystematic risk has been diversified away. Beta measures exactly this non-diversifiable portion. The Trap: (A) is a practical aside, not the CAPM rationale. (B) is empirically false. (C) is incorrect — CAPM is general across asset types. Note: Page 225 provides related beta and systematic-risk context. The CAPM rationale rests on diversification of unsystematic risk inside the market portfolio.
